questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For which one of the following, Bohr model is NOT valid?
questions.explanation: Bohr model is strictly applicable only to single-electron hydrogen-like species. $\text{Ne}^+$ has 9 electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The ratio of contributions made by the electric field and magnetic field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave is ($c = $ speed of light):
questions.explanation: Energy density is equally shared between electric and magnetic fields ($u_E = u_B = \frac{1}{2} u_{\text{total}}$). Ratio of intensity contributions is $1 : 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The Brewster's angle $i_b$ for an air-dielectric interface with $\mu > 1$ should be:
questions.explanation: $\tan i_b = \mu > 1 \implies i_b > 45^\circ$. Since $\mu < \infty$, $45^\circ < i_b < 90^\circ$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A cylinder contains hydrogen gas at pressure of $249\text{ kPa}$ and temperature $27^\circ\text{C}$. Its density is ($R = 8.3\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$):
questions.explanation: $\rho = \frac{P M}{R T} = \frac{(249 \times 10^3) \times (2 \times 10^{-3})}{8.3 \times 300} = 0.2\text{ kg/m}^3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A ray is incident at angle $i$ on small angle prism of angle $A$ and emerges normally ($r_2 = 0$). The angle of incidence is nearly equal to:
questions.explanation: $r_1 + r_2 = A \implies r_1 = A$. Using Snell's law for small angles: $\sin i \approx i = \mu \sin r_1 = \mu A$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two cylinders A and B of equal capacity are connected via stopcock. A has ideal gas at STP; B is evacuated. If thermally insulated and stopcock is suddenly opened, the process is:
questions.explanation: Thermally insulated enclosure implies $Q = 0$ (adiabatic free expansion).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The energy equivalent of $0.5\text{ g}$ of a substance is:
questions.explanation: $E = m c^2 = (0.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg}) \times (3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s})^2 = 4.5 \times 10^{13}\text{ J}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A body weighs $72\text{ N}$ on Earth's surface. What is the gravitational force on it at height $h = R/2$?
questions.explanation: $g' = \frac{g}{(1 + h/R)^2} = \frac{g}{(1 + 1/2)^2} = \frac{4}{9}g \implies W' = 72 \times \frac{4}{9} = 32\text{ N}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The solids which have a negative temperature coefficient of resistance are:
questions.explanation: For both insulators and semiconductors, thermal excitation releases more charge carriers as temperature rises, decreasing resistance ($\alpha < 0$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The phase difference between displacement and acceleration of a particle in simple harmonic motion is:
questions.explanation: $x = A\sin(\omega t)$, $a = -\omega^2 x = \omega^2 A \sin(\omega t + \pi) \implies$ phase difference is $\pi\text{ rad}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A screw gauge has least count $0.01\text{ mm}$ and 50 circular divisions. The pitch of the screw gauge is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Pitch} = \text{Least Count} \times \text{Divisions} = 0.01\text{ mm} \times 50 = 0.5\text{ mm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two guitar strings produce beat frequency $6\text{ Hz}$. When tension in B is slightly decreased, beat frequency increases to $7\text{ Hz}$. If $\nu_A = 530\text{ Hz}$, original frequency of B is:
questions.explanation:
Decreasing tension decreases $
u_B$. Since beat frequency increased from 6 to 7, $
u_B$ was initially lower: $
u_B = 530 - 6 = 524	ext{ Hz}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two particles $5\text{ kg}$ and $10\text{ kg}$ are connected by a rigid $1\text{ m}$ rod. The centre of mass from the $5\text{ kg}$ particle is at distance:
questions.explanation: $x = \frac{10 \times 100}{5 + 10} = \frac{1000}{15} = 66.7\text{ cm} \approx 67\text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Find the torque about origin when force $\vec{F} = 3\hat{j}\text{ N}$ acts on a particle with position vector $\vec{r} = 2\hat{k}\text{ m}$:
questions.explanation: $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = (2\hat{k}) \times (3\hat{j}) = -6\hat{i}\text{ N m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Light of average flux $20\text{ W/cm}^2$ falls normally on area $20\text{ cm}^2$ for 1 minute. Total energy received is:
questions.explanation: $U = \Phi \times A \times t = 20 \times 20 \times 60 = 24000\text{ J} = 24 \times 10^3\text{ J}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A spherical conductor of radius $10\text{ cm}$ has charge $3.2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}$. Electric field at point $15\text{ cm}$ from centre is:
questions.explanation: $E = \frac{k q}{r^2} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 3.2 \times 10^{-7}}{(0.15)^2} = 1.28 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In a volume of $0.2\text{ m}^3$, electric potential is $5\text{ V}$ constant throughout. Electric field magnitude is:
questions.explanation: $E = -\frac{dV}{dr} = 0$ in equipotential regions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The increase in width of depletion region in a p-n junction diode is due to:
questions.explanation: Reverse bias pulls majority charge carriers away from the junction, widening the depletion region.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $40\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is connected to $200\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ ac supply. RMS current is nearly:
questions.explanation: $X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C} = \frac{1}{2\pi \times 50 \times 40 \times 10^{-6}} = 79.58\,\Omega$. $I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{200}{79.58} \approx 2.51\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Mean free path $\lambda$ for gas molecules of diameter $d$ and number density $n$ is:
questions.explanation: Standard kinetic formula: $\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi n d^2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For proper transistor action, which statement is correct?
questions.optionA: Base, emitter and collector should have same doping
questions.optionB: Base, emitter and collector should have same size
questions.optionC: Both emitter and collector junctions are forward biased
questions.optionD: The base region must be very thin and lightly doped
questions.explanation: A thin lightly doped base minimizes electron-hole recombination so majority of carriers reach the collector.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Light of frequency $1.5\nu_0$ is incident. What will be photoelectric current if frequency is halved and intensity doubled?
questions.explanation:
New frequency $
u' = 0.75
u_0 < 
u_0$. Since incident frequency is below threshold frequency, no photoemission occurs ($I = 0$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: When $^{235}_{92}\text{U}$ captures a neutron, it generates $^{89}_{36}\text{Kr}$, 3 neutrons, and:
questions.explanation: Mass conservation: $235 + 1 = 89 + 3(1) + A \implies A = 144$. Charge: $92 = 36 + Z \implies Z = 56$ ($^{144}_{56}\text{Ba}$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Energy to break one bond in DNA is $10^{-20}\text{ J}$. This value in $\text{eV}$ is nearly:
questions.explanation: $E = \frac{10^{-20}\text{ J}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J/eV}} = 0.0625\text{ eV} \approx 0.06\text{ eV}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two masses $4\text{ kg}$ and $6\text{ kg}$ pass over frictionless pulley. Acceleration of system is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Wire of length $L$ changes to $L_1$ when mass $M$ is suspended. Young's modulus $Y$ is:
questions.explanation: $Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} = \frac{M g / A}{(L_1 - L)/L} = \frac{M g L}{A(L_1 - L)}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The average thermal kinetic energy for a mono-atomic gas is ($k_B = $ Boltzmann constant):
questions.explanation: Monoatomic gas has 3 translational degrees of freedom $\implies E = \frac{3}{2} k_B T$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Variation of resistivity ($\rho$) with temperature ($T$) for copper metal is:
questions.optionC: Non-linear curve increasing rapidly with temperature
questions.explanation: For copper at low temperatures, resistivity increases non-linearly with temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Color code bands on resistor: Yellow, Violet, Brown, Gold. Resistance and tolerance are:
questions.explanation: Yellow $= 4$, Violet $= 7$, Brown $= 10^1$, Gold $= \pm 5\% \implies R = 47 \times 10^1\,\Omega = 470\,\Omega \pm 5\%$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In YDSE, if slit separation is halved ($d' = d/2$) and screen distance doubled ($D' = 2D$), fringe width becomes:
questions.explanation: $\beta' = \frac{\lambda D'}{d'} = \frac{\lambda (2D)}{d/2} = 4\left(\frac{\lambda D}{d}\right) = 4\beta$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Capacitance in air is $6\,\mu\text{F}$. With dielectric medium, it becomes $30\,\mu\text{F}$. Permittivity of medium is ($\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}$):
questions.explanation: $K = 30/6 = 5$. $\varepsilon = K \varepsilon_0 = 5 \times (8.85 \times 10^{-12}) = 0.44 \times 10^{-10}\text{ C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Dimensions of mechanical stress are:
questions.explanation: $[\text{Stress}] = \frac{[F]}{[A]} = \frac{[\text{MLT}^{-2}]}{[\text{L}^2]} = [\text{ML}^{-1}\text{T}^{-2}]$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Limit of resolution of telescope with objective diameter $2\text{ m}$ for wavelength $600\text{ nm}$ is:
questions.explanation: $\theta = \frac{1.22 \lambda}{D} = \frac{1.22 \times 600 \times 10^{-9}}{2} = 3.66 \times 10^{-7}\text{ rad}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In LCR circuit, removing L gives phase angle $\pi/3$; removing C gives phase angle $\pi/3$. Power factor of complete LCR circuit is:
questions.explanation: Since $\tan(\pi/3) = X_C/R = X_L/R$, $X_L = X_C$ (resonance). At resonance, $Z = R$ and power factor $\cos\phi = 1.0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Dipole $p = 16 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C m}$ at distance $0.6\text{ m}$ at angle $60^\circ$ to dipole axis has electric potential:
questions.explanation: $V = \frac{k p \cos\theta}{r^2} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 16 \times 10^{-9} \times 0.5}{(0.6)^2} = \frac{72}{0.36} = 200\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: An iron rod of susceptibility $\chi = 599$ in field $1200\text{ A/m}$ has permeability $\mu$ equal to:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A solenoid of length $50\text{ cm}$ with 100 turns carries current $2.5\text{ A}$. Magnetic field at centre is:
questions.explanation: $B = \mu_0 \frac{N}{L} I = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times \frac{100}{0.5} \times 2.5 = 6.28 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Charged particle with drift velocity $7.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m/s}$ in field $3 \times 10^{-10}\text{ V/m}$ has mobility $\mu$ equal to:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Heat required to raise temperature of solid copper spheres of radii $r_1 = 1.5 r_2$ through $1\text{ K}$ is in ratio:
questions.explanation: $Q = m c \Delta T \propto \text{Volume} \propto r^3 \implies \frac{Q_1}{Q_2} = \left(\frac{1.5}{1}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: An electron accelerated through potential $V$ has de Broglie wavelength $1.227 \times 10^{-2}\text{ nm} = 0.1227\text{ Å}$. Potential $V$ is:
questions.explanation: $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ Å} = 0.1227\text{ Å} \implies \sqrt{V} = 100 \implies V = 10^4\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Taking into account significant figures, value of $9.99\text{ m} - 0.0099\text{ m}$ is:
questions.explanation: $9.99$ has 2 decimal places. $9.99 - 0.0099 = 9.9801\text{ m}$, rounded off to 2 decimal places is $9.98\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A ball thrown downward at $20\text{ m/s}$ hits ground at $80\text{ m/s}$. Height of tower is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $v^2 = u^2 + 2gh \implies 80^2 = 20^2 + 2(10)h \implies 6400 - 400 = 20h \implies h = 300\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Capillary tube of radius $r$ holds water mass $5\text{ g}$. Mass of water rising in capillary of radius $2r$ is:
questions.explanation: $m = \rho \pi r^2 h = \rho \pi r^2 (\frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r}) \propto r \implies m' = 2(5\text{ g}) = 10\text{ g}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Metre bridge balances $10\,\Omega$ in right gap at ratio $3 : 2$. If resistance wire length is $1.5\text{ m}$, length of $1\,\Omega$ is:
questions.explanation: $R / 10 = 3/2 \implies R = 15\,\Omega$. Length for $15\,\Omega$ is $1.5\text{ m} \implies$ length for $1\,\Omega$ is $1.5/15 = 0.1\text{ m} = 1.0 \times 10^{-1}\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Truth table for logic circuit with NOT on A and B fed into NOR gate is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: $Y = \overline{\overline{A} + \overline{B}} = A \cdot B$ (De Morgan's theorem: AND gate).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify a molecule which does NOT exist according to Molecular Orbital Theory:
questions.explanation: $\text{He}_2$ has configuration $\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^*_{1s}^2$ with bond order $= \frac{2-2}{2} = 0$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Solubility of $\text{Ni(OH)}_2$ in $0.1\text{ M NaOH}$ ($K_{sp} = 2 \times 10^{-15}$) is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Identify the correct statements:
(a) $\text{CO}_2(g)$ is refrigerant for ice-cream
(b) $\text{C}_{60}$ has 12 six-membered and 20 five-membered rings
(c) ZSM-5 converts alcohols into gasoline
(d) $\text{CO}$ is colourless and odourless
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Dry ice (solid $\text{CO}_2$) is the refrigerant (not gas). $\text{C}_{60}$ has 20 six-membered and 12 five-membered rings. (c) and (d) are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Hydrolysis of sucrose has $K_c = 2 \times 10^{13}$ at $300\text{ K}$. Value of $\Delta_r G^\circ$ is:
questions.explanation: $\Delta_r G^\circ = -RT \ln K_c = -8.314 \times 300 \times \ln(2 \times 10^{13})$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify compound X in sequence: $\text{Toluene} \xrightarrow{\text{Cl}_2/h\nu} X \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}, 373\text{ K}} \text{Benzaldehyde}$:
questions.explanation: Side-chain dichlorination yields benzal chloride $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHCl}_2$, which hydrolyzes to benzaldehyde.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT match of element name and IUPAC official name:
questions.optionD: Unununnium - Darmstadtium (111 is Roentgenium; 110 is Darmstadtium)
questions.explanation: Element 111 (Unununium) is Roentgenium (Rg). Darmstadtium is element 110.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: BCC lattice has edge length $a = 288\text{ pm}$. Atomic radius $r$ is:
questions.explanation: In BCC, body diagonal $4r = \sqrt{3}a \implies r = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 288\text{ pm}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following sets of molecules will have ZERO dipole moment?
questions.optionD: Boron trifluoride, beryllium difluoride, carbon dioxide, 1,4-dichlorobenzene
questions.explanation: $\text{BF}_3$ (trigonal planar), $\text{BeF}_2$ (linear), $\text{CO}_2$ (linear), and 1,4-dichlorobenzene (symmetrical trans) all have $\mu = 0$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: On electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid using inert Platinum electrodes, product obtained at anode is:
questions.explanation: Oxidation of water occurs at anode: $2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{H}^+ + 4e^-$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Reaction between acetone and methylmagnesium chloride followed by acid hydrolysis gives:
questions.explanation: $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgCl} \to (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which oxoacid of sulphur contains a peroxo linkage ($-O-O-$)?
questions.explanation: Marshall's acid $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$ has structure $\text{HO-SO}_2-\text{O-O-SO}_2-\text{OH}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following amines will give the positive Carbylamine test (isocyanide test)?
questions.explanation: Carbylamine test is specific for primary ($1^\circ$) aliphatic and aromatic amines.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The calculated spin-only magnetic moment of $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ion ($d^4$, 4 unpaired electrons) is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct thermodynamic conditions for free expansion of ideal gas under adiabatic conditions are:
questions.explanation: Adiabatic implies $q = 0$. Free expansion against vacuum implies $w = 0$. By first law, $\Delta U = 0 \implies \Delta T = 0$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Freezing point depression constant $K_f = 5.12\text{ K kg/mol}$. Depression for $0.078\text{ m}$ non-electrolyte in benzene is:
questions.explanation: $\Delta T_f = K_f \cdot m = 5.12 \times 0.078 = 0.399\text{ K} \approx 0.40\text{ K}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Number of Faradays required to produce $20\text{ g}$ calcium from molten $\text{CaCl}_2$ ($M = 40\text{ g/mol}$) is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Ca}^{2+} + 2e^- \to \text{Ca}$. $40\text{ g}$ requires $2\text{ F} \implies 20\text{ g}$ requires $1\text{ F}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Reaction between benzaldehyde and acetophenone in presence of dilute $\text{NaOH}$ is:
questions.explanation: Reaction between aromatic aldehyde (no $\alpha$-H) and ketone with $\alpha$-H is Claisen-Schmidt cross aldol condensation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Paper chromatography is an example of:
questions.explanation: Water trapped in paper fibres acts as stationary liquid phase, making it partition chromatography.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An increase in the concentration of reactants leads to a direct increase in:
questions.explanation: Higher concentration increases number of molecules per unit volume, increasing collision frequency.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A cylinder contains $7\text{ g } \text{N}_2$ and $8\text{ g Ar}$ at total pressure $27\text{ bar}$. Partial pressure of $\text{N}_2$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the correct metallurgical statement:
questions.optionA: Wrought iron is impure with 4% carbon
questions.optionB: Blister copper appearance is due to evolution of $\text{CO}_2$
questions.optionC: Nickel is refined by Van Arkel method
questions.optionD: Pig iron can be cast and moulded into a variety of shapes
questions.explanation: Pig iron (high carbon) is remelted with scrap to make cast iron, which is easily moulded.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Tert-butyl carbocation is more stable than sec-butyl carbocation because of:
questions.explanation: Tert-butyl carbocation has 9 $\alpha$-hydrogens exhibiting extensive hyperconjugative stabilization compared to 5 in sec-butyl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a CATIONIC detergent?
questions.explanation: Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide contains quaternary ammonium cation with long alkyl chain.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Elimination reaction of 2-bromopentane to form pent-2-ene is categorized as:
(a) $\beta$-elimination, (b) Follows Zaitsev rule, (c) Dehydrohalogenation, (d) Dehydration
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Loss of H from $\beta$-carbon and Br from $\alpha$-carbon is $\beta$-elimination and dehydrohalogenation following Zaitsev's rule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The liquid mixture which shows POSITIVE deviation from Raoult’s law is:
questions.explanation: Acetone breaks hydrogen bonds between ethanol molecules, increasing vapour pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct spectrochemical series order of increasing ligand field strength is:
questions.explanation: Spectrochemical series: $\text{I}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{SCN}^- < \text{Cl}^- < \text{F}^- < \text{OH}^- < \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{en} < \text{CN}^- < \text{CO}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a BASIC amino acid?
questions.explanation: Lysine and Arginine possess basic amino side chains.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When $\text{HCl}$ gas is passed through a solution of $\text{CaCl}_2, \text{MgCl}_2$ and $\text{NaCl}$, which compound crystallises out?
questions.explanation: Common ion effect ($[\text{Cl}^-]$) exceeds ionic product of $\text{NaCl}$; $\text{CaCl}_2$ and $\text{MgCl}_2$ are much more soluble and remain in solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following is natural rubber (natural polymer)?
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which statement is NOT correct about Carbon Monoxide ($\text{CO}$)?
questions.optionB: It reduces oxygen-carrying capacity of blood
questions.optionC: Carboxyhaemoglobin is less stable than oxyhaemoglobin (It is 300x more stable)
questions.optionD: It is produced by incomplete combustion
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin is about 300 times more stable than oxyhaemoglobin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Sucrose on enzymatic or acidic hydrolysis gives equimolar mixture of:
questions.explanation: Sucrose hydrolysis yields $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose and $\beta$-D-fructofuranose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which metal ion activates ATP-producing glycolytic enzymes and works with $\text{Na}^+$ in nerve impulses?
questions.explanation: Potassium ions activate pyruvate kinase and participate in sodium-potassium ATPase pump.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which sample has the MAXIMUM number of atoms?
questions.explanation: Number of atoms $= \frac{w}{M} \times N_A$. Lithium ($M=7$) has highest moles $= 1/7\text{ mol} \approx 0.143 N_A$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Number of protons, neutrons and electrons in $^{175}_{71}\text{Lu}$ are respectively:
questions.explanation: $Z = 71$ protons and electrons. Neutrons $N = 175 - 71 = 104$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Change in oxidation number of carbon in: $\text{CH}_4 + 4\text{Cl}_2 \to \text{CCl}_4 + 4\text{HCl}$ is:
questions.explanation: In $\text{CH}_4$, C is $-4$. In $\text{CCl}_4$, C is $+4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding transition metals:
questions.optionA: $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($d^4$) is stronger reducing agent than $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6$) in water
questions.optionB: Transition metals have high catalytic activity due to variable oxidation states
questions.optionC: Interstitial compounds form when small non-metal atoms are trapped in metal lattice
questions.optionD: Oxidation states of Cr in $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ and $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ are not the same (Both are +6)
questions.explanation: Chromium is in $+6$ oxidation state in both chromate and dichromate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For bond formation reaction: $2\text{Cl}(g) \to \text{Cl}_2(g)$, the thermodynamic signs are:
questions.explanation: Bond formation releases energy ($\Delta H < 0$) and 2 moles of gas combine into 1 mole ($\Delta S < 0$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Measuring Zeta potential is useful in determining which property of colloidal solutions?
questions.optionC: Stability of colloidal particles (Repulsion prevents coagulation)
questions.explanation: Zeta potential measures electrical potential on double layer; high zeta potential prevents agglomeration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Urea decomposes to form $\text{NH}_3$. When passed through $\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)$, deep blue complex C formed is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4\text{NH}_3 \to [\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ (deep blue solution).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Inorganic chemistry):
(a) $\text{CO} + \text{H}_2$, (b) Temporary hardness of water, (c) $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$, (d) $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$
(i) $\text{Mg(HCO}_3)_2 + \text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$, (ii) Electron deficient hydride, (iii) Synthesis gas, (iv) Non-planar open book structure
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Syn gas = (iii), Hardness = bicarbonates (i), $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$ = electron deficient (ii), $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ = open book (iv).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Oxides with Acid-Base Nature:
(a) $\text{CO}$, (b) $\text{BaO}$, (c) $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, (d) $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$
(i) Basic, (ii) Neutral, (iii) Acidic, (iv) Amphoteric
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: $\text{CO}$ = Neutral (ii), $\text{BaO}$ = Basic (i), $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ = Amphoteric (iv), $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$ = Acidic (iii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Rate constant for first order reaction is $4.606 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}$. Time required to reduce $2.0\text{ g}$ to $0.2\text{ g}$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which alkene on ozonolysis gives methanal ($\text{HCHO}$) as one product?
questions.explanation: Terminal alkenes ($=\text{CH}_2$) produce methanal upon ozonolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which alkane CANNOT be synthesized in good yield by Wurtz reaction?
questions.optionC: n-Heptane (Unsymmetrical with odd number of 7 carbons)
questions.explanation: Wurtz reaction gives poor yields for odd-carbon alkanes like n-heptane due to mixture of 3 different cross products.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Anisole ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OCH}_3$) on cleavage with concentrated $\text{HI}$ gives:
questions.explanation: Phenyl-oxygen bond has partial double bond character due to resonance and does not break; nucleophile $\text{I}^-$ attacks methyl group.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an attribute of a population?
questions.explanation: Sex ratio, natality, and mortality are population attributes; species interaction involves community-level dynamics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The process of cell growth is MAXIMUM during:
questions.explanation: In the log/exponential phase, cell division and biomass accumulation proceed at maximal geometric rate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The roots that originate from the base of the stem in monocots (like wheat) are:
questions.explanation: In monocots, short-lived primary root is replaced by a cluster of fibrous roots originating from stem base.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Diseases with Causative Pathogens:
(a) Typhoid, (b) Pneumonia, (c) Filariasis, (d) Malaria
(i) Wuchereria, (ii) Plasmodium, (iii) Salmonella typhi, (iv) Haemophilus influenzae
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Typhoid = Salmonella (iii), Pneumonia = Haemophilus (iv), Filariasis = Wuchereria (i), Malaria = Plasmodium (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In which ART techniques are EMBRYOS transferred to assist infertile females who cannot conceive?
questions.explanation: ZIFT (Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer up to 8 blastomeres) and IUT (Intra-Uterine Transfer >8 blastomeres) transfer embryos.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the WRONG statement regarding ABO blood group gene I:
questions.optionA: The gene I has three alleles ($I^A, I^B, i$)
questions.optionB: A person will have only two of the three alleles
questions.optionC: When $I^A$ and $I^B$ are present together, they express same type of sugar
questions.optionD: Allele 'i' does not produce any surface sugar
questions.explanation: $I^A$ and $I^B$ are codominant and produce distinct sugar polymers (A and B antigens), not the same sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Choose the CORRECT enzyme-function pair:
questions.optionA: Ligases - Join two DNA fragments together
questions.optionD: Exonucleases - Make internal cuts in DNA
questions.explanation: DNA ligases seal phosphodiester nicks to join DNA molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the CORRECT genetic match:
questions.optionC: Sickle cell anaemia - Autosomal recessive trait, chromosome 11
questions.explanation: Sickle cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by $\text{GAG} \to \text{GUG}$ mutation on chromosome 11.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Animal Kingdom Features:
(a) Gregarious pest, (b) Adult radial and larva bilateral symmetry, (c) Book lungs, (d) Bioluminescence
(i) Asterias, (ii) Scorpion, (iii) Ctenoplana, (iv) Locusta
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Locusta = Gregarious pest (iv), Asterias = Echinoderm symmetry (i), Scorpion = Book lungs (ii), Ctenoplana = Bioluminescent ctenophore (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The infectious stage of Plasmodium that enters human body through mosquito bite is:
questions.explanation: Infective sporozoites inoculated with mosquito saliva migrate to liver cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify substances having glycosidic bond and peptide bond respectively in their structure:
questions.explanation: Inulin has glycosidic bonds between fructose units; insulin has peptide bonds connecting amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Plant structures which consist of two generations - one within the other:
(a) Pollen grains inside anther
(b) Germinated pollen grain with 2 male gametes
(c) Seed inside fruit
(d) Embryo sac inside ovule
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Pollen grain (gametophyte) develops within anther (sporophyte); embryo sac (gametophyte) develops within ovule (sporophyte).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The products of reaction catalyzed by Nitrogenase in legume root nodules are:
questions.optionD: Ammonia and hydrogen ($\text{N}_2 + 8e^- + 8	ext{H}^+ + 16	ext{ATP} \to 2	ext{NH}_3 + 	ext{H}_2$)
questions.explanation: Nitrogenase reaction yields $2\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2 + 16\text{ADP} + 16\text{P}_i$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the correct statement with regard to $G_1$ phase (Gap 1) of interphase:
questions.optionA: DNA synthesis or replication takes place
questions.optionB: Reorganisation of all cell components takes place
questions.optionC: Cell is metabolically active, grows continuously but does not replicate its DNA
questions.explanation: In $G_1$ phase, cell is metabolically active and synthesizes proteins/RNA for growth without DNA replication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Cuboidal epithelium with a brush border of microvilli is found in:
questions.explanation: PCT cells are simple cuboidal with microvilli brush borders to maximize reabsorption surface.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about bacterial inclusion bodies is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: They are not bound by any membrane
questions.optionB: These are involved in ingestion of food particles (They are non-living storage granules)
questions.optionC: They lie free in the cytoplasm
questions.optionD: These represent reserve material in cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Inclusion bodies store phosphate, cyanophycin, or glycogen granules and are not phagocytic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids in eukaryotic cells is:
questions.explanation: Post-translational glycosylation of proteins and lipids occurs in Golgi cisternae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In gel electrophoresis, separated DNA fragments are visualized using:
questions.explanation: EtBr staining fluoresces orange under UV radiation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the WRONG statement with reference to oxygen transport:
questions.optionA: Binding of $\text{O}_2$ with Hb is mainly related to $pO_2$
questions.optionC: Higher $H^+$ concentration in alveoli favours oxyhaemoglobin formation (Alveoli have low $H^+$/high pH)
questions.optionD: Low $pCO_2$ in alveoli favours oxyhaemoglobin formation
questions.explanation: High $H^+$ (acidosis) promotes oxygen dissociation (Bohr effect), whereas alveoli have low $H^+$ promoting binding.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Ray florets of Sunflower have:
questions.explanation: Ray florets in Asteraceae have epigynous flowers with inferior ovary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Specific palindromic recognition sequence cleaved by EcoRI is:
questions.explanation: EcoRI recognizes $5'-\text{GAATTC}-3'$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the WRONG statement with regard to Restriction Enzymes:
questions.optionA: Each enzyme functions by inspecting length of DNA sequence
questions.optionB: They cut DNA at palindromic sites
questions.optionC: They are useful in genetic engineering
questions.optionD: Sticky ends can be joined by DNA ligases
questions.explanation: All statements are technically valid; official answer key marked option 4 (or 1 depending on context of ligase function vs RE function).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is put into Anaerobic sludge digester for sewage treatment?
questions.explanation: Settled activated sludge flocs are pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters where methanogens digest them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct events that occur during inspiration in human breathing:
(a) Contraction of diaphragm
(b) Contraction of external intercostals
(c) Pulmonary volume decreases
(d) Intra-pulmonary pressure increases
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Diaphragm and external intercostals contract, expanding thoracic cavity and dropping intrapulmonary pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A decapitated cockroach can survive for several days because:
questions.optionC: Head holds only a small part of nervous system while rest lies along ventral nerve cord
questions.optionD: Head holds 1/3rd of nervous system along dorsal part
questions.explanation: The nervous system of cockroach is spread throughout body segments along ventral nerve cord.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Which statements are TRUE for Phylum Chordata?
(a) In Urochordata, notochord extends head to tail throughout life
(b) In Vertebrata, notochord is embryonic and replaced by vertebral column
(c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow
(d) Chordata divided into Hemichordata, Tunicata, Cephalochordata
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Statements (b) and (c) are true chordate characteristics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Biotechnology Organisms:
(a) Bacillus thuringiensis, (b) Thermus aquaticus, (c) Agrobacterium tumefaciens, (d) Salmonella typhimurium
(i) Cloning vector (Ti plasmid), (ii) First rDNA molecule, (iii) Taq DNA polymerase, (iv) Cry proteins
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Bt = Cry (iv), Taq = Polymerase (iii), Agrobacterium = Vector (i), Salmonella = First rDNA (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Plant Micronutrients:
(a) Iron, (b) Zinc, (c) Boron, (d) Manganese
(i) Photolysis of water, (ii) Pollen germination, (iii) Chlorophyll synthesis, (iv) IAA auxin biosynthesis
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Iron = Chlorophyll synthesis (iii), Zinc = Auxin/IAA (iv), Boron = Pollen germination (ii), Manganese = Photolysis (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT statement about secondary xylem:
questions.optionA: Heartwood does not conduct water but gives mechanical support
questions.optionB: Sapwood is involved in water conduction from root to leaf
questions.optionC: Sapwood is the innermost secondary xylem (Heartwood is innermost; sapwood is peripheral)
questions.optionD: Heartwood is dark due to deposition of tannins and resins
questions.explanation: Heartwood forms the central core while sapwood (alburnum) is peripheral.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Biomolecules:
(a) Inhibitor of catalytic activity, (b) Possess peptide bonds, (c) Fungal cell wall, (d) Secondary metabolite alkaloid/toxin
(i) Ricin, (ii) Malonate, (iii) Chitin, (iv) Collagen
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Malonate = Succinate dehydrogenase inhibitor (ii), Collagen = Protein (iv), Chitin = Fungal wall (iii), Ricin = Toxin (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Meiotic division of secondary oocyte is completed:
questions.optionD: At the time of fusion of sperm with ovum (sperm entry)
questions.explanation: Entry of sperm induces breakdown of MPF and activates APC, completing Meiosis II.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: According to Robert May, global species diversity estimate is about:
questions.explanation: Robert May estimated global species richness at approximately 7 million.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The very first phase of translation (protein synthesis) is:
questions.explanation: Amino acids are first activated and attached to cognate tRNA by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which region of the globe exhibits HIGHEST species diversity on Earth?
questions.explanation: Tropical Amazon rainforest in South America possesses the highest biodiversity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement about Insulin is NOT correct?
questions.optionA: In man, insulin is synthesised as proinsulin
questions.optionC: Functional insulin has A and B chains linked by hydrogen bonds (Linked by disulfide bonds)
questions.optionD: Genetically engineered insulin is produced in E. coli
questions.explanation: A and B chains of mature insulin are interconnected by two interchain disulfide bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Transverse section of plant shows:
(a) Scattered vascular bundles in bundle sheath
(b) Large parenchymatous ground tissue
(c) Conjoint closed bundles
(d) Phloem parenchyma absent
Identify plant and organ:
questions.explanation: Scattered conjoint closed vascular bundles with absent phloem parenchyma are hallmarks of monocot stem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Vertebrates:
(a) 6-15 pairs of gill slits, (b) Heterocercal caudal fin, (c) Air bladder, (d) Poison sting
(i) Trygon, (ii) Cyclostomes, (iii) Chondrichthyes, (iv) Osteichthyes
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Cyclostomes = 6-15 gill pairs (ii), Chondrichthyes = Heterocercal tail (iii), Osteichthyes = Air bladder (iv), Trygon = Poison sting (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In Miller's experiment, amino acids were produced in a spark discharge flask containing:
questions.explanation: Stanley Miller created primitive reducing atmosphere of $\text{CH}_4 : \text{NH}_3 : \text{H}_2$ ($2:1:2$) and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ vapor at $800^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Embryological support for evolution proposed by Ernst Haeckel was disapproved by:
questions.explanation: Von Baer observed that general embryonic features appear before specialized characters, disproving biogenetic law.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The process responsible for guttation (liquid water loss from hydathodes) at night is:
questions.explanation: Positive hydrostatic root pressure forces water droplets through hydathodes when transpiration is low.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Secondary metabolites like nicotine, strychnine and caffeine are produced by plants primarily for:
questions.explanation: Alkaloids act as chemical deterrents and toxins against predators and herbivores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Oxygenation activity of RuBisCO in photorespiration ($	ext{C}_2$ cycle) leads to formation of:
questions.optionB: 1 molecule of 3-C PGA and 1 molecule of 2-C Phosphoglycolate
questions.explanation: $\text{RuBP} + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{RuBisCO}} 1\,\text{PGA (3C)} + 1\,\text{Phosphoglycolate (2C)}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Bt cotton developed by introducing Cry toxin genes from Bacillus thuringiensis is resistant to:
questions.explanation: CryIAc and CryIIAb endotoxins provide resistance against cotton bollworms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Which of the following examples have evolved due to anthropogenic (human-induced) action?
(a) Darwin's Finches, (b) Herbicide resistant weeds, (c) Drug resistant microbes, (d) Domesticated animal breeds
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Pesticide resistance, antibiotic resistance, and artificial dog breeding are anthropogenic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the WRONG statement with reference to immunity:
questions.optionA: Active immunity produces antibodies in host upon antigen exposure
questions.optionB: Passive immunity involves administering pre-formed antibodies
questions.optionC: Active immunity is quick and gives immediate full response (Active immunity is slow)
questions.explanation: Active immunity requires lag time to activate clonal expansion and is slow compared to passive immunity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The new sheep breed 'Hisardale' in Punjab was developed by cross-breeding:
questions.optionC: Cross breeding (Bikaneri ewes and Merino rams)
questions.explanation: Cross-breeding superior females of one breed with superior males of another breed produced Hisardale.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the CORRECT anatomical statement about human digestive tract:
questions.optionC: Ileum is a highly coiled part of small intestine
questions.explanation: Small intestine consists of C-shaped duodenum, coiled jejunum, and highly coiled ileum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Microbes with Commercial Products:
(a) Clostridium butylicum, (b) Trichoderma polysporum, (c) Monascus purpureus, (d) Aspergillus niger
(i) Cyclosporin-A, (ii) Butyric acid, (iii) Citric acid, (iv) Statin (Blood cholesterol lowering agent)
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Clostridium = Butyric (ii), Trichoderma = Cyclosporin A (i), Monascus = Statin (iv), Aspergillus = Citric (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Presence of which conditions in urine is indicative of Diabetes Mellitus?
questions.explanation: Glycosuria (glucose in urine) and ketonuria (ketone bodies in urine) are classic clinical signs of diabetes mellitus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Floridean starch found in Rhodophyceae (red algae) is structural homolog of:
questions.explanation: Floridean starch is branched $\alpha$-glucan structurally very similar to amylopectin and glycogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the option including ALL Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs):
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea (bacterial), Syphilis (bacterial), and Genital herpes (viral) are all STIs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Meiosis Prophase-I Substages:
(a) Zygotene, (b) Pachytene, (c) Diplotene, (d) Diakinesis
(i) Terminalization, (ii) Chiasmata appearance, (iii) Crossing over, (iv) Synapsis of homologues
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Zygotene = Synapsis (iv), Pachytene = Crossing over (iii), Diplotene = Chiasmata (ii), Diakinesis = Terminalization (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following pairs represents UNICELLULAR protein-rich algae?
questions.explanation: Chlorella and Spirulina are unicellular algae rich in proteins used as food supplements by space travelers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Ovulation (release of ovum from mature Graafian follicle) is triggered by:
questions.optionA: High concentration of Estrogen / LH surge
questions.explanation: Peak estrogen induces rapid secretion of LH (LH surge), which ruptures the Graafian follicle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Biotechnology Applications:
(a) Bt cotton, (b) ADA deficiency, (c) RNAi, (d) PCR
(i) Gene therapy, (ii) Cellular defence in all eukaryotes, (iii) Detection of HIV infection, (iv) Bacillus thuringiensis
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Bt cotton = Bacillus (iv), ADA = Gene therapy (i), RNAi = Cellular defence (ii), PCR = HIV detection (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Montreal Protocol was signed in 1987 to control:
questions.optionB: Emission of Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS / CFCs)
questions.explanation: Montreal Protocol was ratified to phase out production of chlorofluorocarbons and ozone-depleting substances.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about Viroids?
questions.optionA: They have RNA with protein coat
questions.optionB: They have free low MW RNA without protein coat
questions.optionC: They have DNA with protein coat
questions.optionD: They have free DNA without protein coat
questions.explanation: Discovered by T.O. Diener, viroids are infectious free RNA molecules lacking a capsid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Half-inferior ovary (Perigynous flower) is found in:
questions.explanation: Plum, rose, and peach have perigynous flowers with half-inferior ovary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The enzyme Enterokinase secreted by intestinal mucosa activates:
questions.explanation: Enterokinase activates pancreatic trypsinogen to trypsin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Trophic Levels in Grassland:
(a) Fourth trophic level ($T_4$), (b) Second trophic level ($T_2$), (c) First trophic level ($T_1$), (d) Third trophic level ($T_3$)
(i) Crow, (ii) Vulture, (iii) Rabbit, (iv) Grass
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: $T_1$ = Grass (iv), $T_2$ = Rabbit (iii), $T_3$ = Crow (i), $T_4$ = Vulture (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: How many true-breeding pea plant varieties (contrasting trait pairs) did Mendel select?
questions.explanation: Mendel selected 14 true-breeding pea plant varieties representing 7 character pairs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Ear Anatomy:
(a) Organ of Corti, (b) Cochlea, (c) Eustachian tube, (d) Stapes
(i) Equalizes pressure between middle ear and pharynx, (ii) Coiled labyrinth, (iii) Attached to oval window, (iv) Located on basilar membrane
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Organ of Corti = Basilar membrane (iv), Cochlea = Coiled labyrinth (ii), Eustachian tube = (i), Stapes = Oval window (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In aquatic plants like Water Hyacinth and Water Lily, pollination is carried out by:
questions.optionA: Insects or Wind (Flowers emerge above water level)
questions.explanation: In water hyacinth and water lily, flowers emerge above water surface and are pollinated by insects or wind.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Spraying which plant growth regulator increases sugarcane stem elongation and yield by 20 tonnes/acre?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins induce internodal elongation in sugarcane stems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In non-cyclic light reaction, Plastoquinone (PQ) transfers electrons from:
questions.explanation: Plastoquinone accepts electrons from primary acceptor of PS-II and transfers them to Cytochrome $b_6f$ complex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an inhibitory substance governing seed dormancy?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins stimulate amylase synthesis to break seed dormancy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The enzyme that facilitates unwinding / opening of DNA helix during transcription is:
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase unwinds the DNA duplex to form transcription bubble.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following would help in prevention of diuresis (water loss)?
questions.optionA: More water reabsorption due to undersecretion of ADH
questions.optionB: Reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and water from renal tubules due to Aldosterone
questions.explanation: Aldosterone acts on DCT to reabsorb $\text{Na}^+$ and water, concentrating urine and preventing diuresis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In relation to Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) and Net Primary Productivity (NPP):
questions.optionA: GPP is always less than NPP
questions.optionB: GPP is always more than NPP ($	ext{GPP} - R = 	ext{NPP}$)
questions.explanation: Gross primary productivity is total organic matter produced, which is always greater than net after respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Reproductive Endocrine Structures:
(a) Placenta, (b) Zona pellucida, (c) Bulbourethral glands, (d) Leydig cells
(i) Androgens, (ii) hCG / Estrogens, (iii) Glycoprotein layer of ovum, (iv) Lubrication of penis
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Placenta = hCG (ii), Zona pellucida = Ovum layer (iii), Bulbourethral = Lubrication (iv), Leydig = Testosterone (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Strobili or cones containing sporangia are found in:
questions.explanation: Equisetum and Selaginella produce distinct apical compact strobili/cones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Dividing cells exit the cell cycle and enter quiescent vegetative $G_0$ stage at the end of:
questions.explanation: Cells that do not divide further exit $G_1$ phase into inactive $G_0$ stage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Flippers of Penguins (birds) and Dolphins (mammals) are classic examples of:
questions.explanation: Convergent evolution results in analogous structures with similar functions in distantly related taxa.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If distance between base pairs is $0.34\text{ nm}$ and total base pairs in human diploid cell is $6.6 \times 10^9\text{ bp}$, DNA length is:
questions.explanation: Length $= (6.6 \times 10^9) \times (0.34 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}) = 2.244\text{ m} \approx 2.2\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The QRS complex in a standard human electrocardiogram (ECG) represents:
questions.explanation: P wave represents atrial depolarization; QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Leukocytes:
(a) Eosinophils, (b) Basophils, (c) Neutrophils, (d) Lymphocytes
(i) Immune response (B & T cells), (ii) Phagocytosis, (iii) Release histaminase, (iv) Release histamine and heparin
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Eosinophils = Histaminase (iii), Basophils = Histamine (iv), Neutrophils = Phagocytic (ii), Lymphocytes = Antibodies (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about DNA Watson-Crick pairing is CORRECT?
questions.optionA: Adenine pairs with thymine through two H-bonds
questions.optionB: Adenine pairs with thymine through one H-bond
questions.optionC: Adenine pairs with thymine through three H-bonds
questions.optionD: Adenine does not pair with thymine
questions.explanation: Adenine pairs with Thymine via 2 hydrogen bonds ($A=T$); Guanine pairs with Cytosine via 3 hydrogen bonds ($G\equiv C$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The sequence in a plasmid vector that controls the copy number of linked DNA is:
questions.explanation: The ori sequence initiates replication and regulates copy number of cloned vector DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the BASIC amino acid from the following:
questions.explanation: Lysine and Arginine are positively charged basic amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Endocrine Disorders:
(a) Pituitary gland, (b) Thyroid gland, (c) Adrenal gland, (d) Pancreas
(i) Graves' disease, (ii) Diabetes mellitus, (iii) Diabetes insipidus (ADH deficiency), (iv) Addison's disease (adrenal cortex deficiency)
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Pituitary = Diabetes insipidus (iii), Thyroid = Graves (i), Adrenal = Addison (iv), Pancreas = Diabetes mellitus (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the CORRECT endocrine statement:
questions.optionA: Glucocorticoids (cortisol) stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis
questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids promote gluconeogenesis to elevate blood glucose level.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which is the MOST ABUNDANT protein in the animal world?
questions.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in animals; RuBisCO is the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Experimental verification of Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance using Drosophila was conducted by:
questions.explanation: T.H. Morgan established link between chromosomes and sex-linked traits using fruit flies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Human Skeleton Parts:
(a) Floating ribs, (b) Acromion process, (c) Scapula, (d) Glenoid cavity
(i) Between 2nd and 7th ribs on dorsal thorax, (ii) Articulates with head of humerus, (iii) Articulates with clavicle, (iv) 11th and 12th ribs not connected to sternum
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Floating ribs = 11th/12th (iv), Acromion = Clavicle (iii), Scapula = Dorsal 2nd-7th (i), Glenoid = Humerus head (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Number of substrate-level phosphorylations (GTP synthesis) in ONE turn of citric acid (Krebs) cycle is:
questions.explanation: During conversion of Succinyl-CoA to succinate, one molecule of GTP is synthesized by substrate-level phosphorylation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs during which stage of prophase I?
questions.explanation: In diplotene, the synaptonemal complex dissolves, leaving homologous chromosomes joined only at chiasmata.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, and ACOELOMATE animals are exemplified by:
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are bilateral, triploblastic, and lack a body cavity (acoelomate).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The body of the ovule is fused with the funicle at the point called:
questions.explanation: Hilum represents the junction where the ovule body attaches to the funicle stalk.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Mucus-secreting Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are modified:
questions.explanation: Goblet cells are specialized glandular columnar cells secreting protective mucus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Snow-blindness in high altitude and polar regions is caused by:
questions.optionB: Inflammation of cornea due to high dose of UV-B radiation
questions.explanation: High-energy UV-B radiation penetrates thin ozone at poles and induces acute corneal inflammation (snow-blindness).
